A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAMWISE. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections 6–11 are readable and support reliable matching across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original RVOS benchmark results, component ablations, and qualitative segmentation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds RoBERTa results, adaptation-strategy comparisons, window-size experiments, and image-segmentation validation.

M1.justification: v2 adds a frozen RoBERTa text-encoder variant with 4.9M trainable parameters alongside CLIP-B with 4.2M. The CMT/HSA architecture, contextual and motion prompts, CME procedure, and training losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use MeViS, Ref-YouTube-VOS, Ref-DAVIS17, and RefCOCO/+/g. The new image-segmentation validation in Table 8 uses the image datasets and referring-segmentation task already present in v1 pretraining; it adds validation protocols and results within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds TCE-RVOS and MUTR while removing URVOS, LBDT, HTML, SgMg, and TempCD. New Table 4 compares full fine-tuning, LoRA, and AdaptFormer against CMT; Table 8 compares image segmentation against MagNet and VISA. The two GroundingDINO+SAM2 baselines were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Reported RefCOCO pretraining increases from 2 to 6 epochs and Ref-YouTube-VOS fine-tuning from 2 to 4, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun. New settings include RoBERTa, ResNet-50 comparator configurations, 4/6/8/12-frame windows, and RefCOCO validation with mIoU. Default T=8 and the video metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds adaptation-strategy controls in Table 4 and window-length sensitivity in Table 6. Conversely, Table 2 removes the isolated motion-prompt contrast, and v1 Figure 10's qualitative comparison against SAM2 baselines disappears. Existing CME case studies and adapter-count/width analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains CLIP-B J&F scores of 48.3/67.2/68.5 and adds RoBERTa scores of 49.5/69.2/70.6 for MeViS/Ref-YouTube-VOS/Ref-DAVIS17 under the revised configuration. Tables 4 and 6–8 add adaptation, window, comparator, and image-segmentation results; Table 2 drops the 53.5 row. The new Ref-DAVIS17 entry is internally inconsistent: its listed J=67.4 and F=74.5 average to 70.95, not 70.6.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 retain the same substantive attention, adaptation, mask-fusion, and self-supervision formulations. Changes such as Fdec becoming Ddec and assignment symbols becoming := are notation corrections; no new theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion revise the parameter-overhead claim from 4.2M to less than 5M, accommodating the RoBERTa variant. The central claims concerning text-prompted SAM2, temporal adaptation, tracking-bias correction, and state-of-the-art performance remain.

C2.justification: v2 discusses CLIP's smaller size versus RoBERTa's reported performance, explains the limited benefit of increasing the window from 8 to 12 frames, and argues that CMT also supports image segmentation. The earlier tracking-bias interpretation remains, while the separately supported benefit of the motion prompt is no longer discussed.

D1.justification: v2 identifies comparator text encoders and specifies CLIP-B for ablations. It newly reports approximately 150 GB GPU memory and 2 A100s for 18 hours for MeViS fine-tuning, versus 8 A100s for 26 hours for full fine-tuning. The original-resolution evaluation statement and conditional trained-model release promise are removed. Both abstracts already provide the same code URL.

R1.justification: References are added for AdaptFormer, LoRA, RoBERTa, MagNet, TCE-RVOS, and MUTR; the LBDT and T5 references disappear. These changes principally support expanded experiments, while the related-work organization and claimed novelty relative to SAM-based approaches remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and terminology edits, including replacing modality 'contamination' with interaction or enrichment, shortening descriptions, updating the supplementary outline, and adding acknowledgements. Most explanations and the section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The experimental displays are substantially revised: Table 1 separates visual and text encoders, Table 2 replaces motion-prompt sections with a CME column, and Tables 4 and 6–8 introduce new comparisons. Figure 3 is visually refreshed and the supplement is reformatted. v1 Figure 10 is removed; v1 Figure 11 is retained as v2 Figure 10.

improvement.justification: The adaptation controls, window-size evidence, image validation, and GPU-cost disclosures provide a limited improvement in empirical support and transparency. Benefits are tempered by removal of the isolated motion-prompt ablation and inconsistencies in new results: the Ref-DAVIS17 aggregate disagrees with its components, and the claimed 2.9-point advantage over VISA is only 1.2 points in Table 1. These issues limit confidence in precise margins without eliminating the value of the added evidence.
